name: Ankylosed Spine Fracture
definition: Spinal fracture through a rigid ankylosed spine in conditions such as ankylosing spondylitis or DISH; these injuries are often unstable after minor trauma.

typical: New focal spinal pain after minor trauma

redFlags.item: Minor trauma with new severe pain

investigations.principle: CT has a major role because radiographs can miss fractures; MRI assesses neural and ligamentous injury.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when the condition-specific question requires soft-tissue, neural, marrow or occult-injury assessment.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs/CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: These injuries often require stabilization because of long-lever-arm instability.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Modern fracture instability assessment takes priority.

patientEducation.summary: Spinal fracture through a rigid ankylosed spine in conditions such as ankylosing spondylitis or DISH; these injuries are often unstable after minor trauma.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for major trauma, acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
